deliverables: Secondary marketplace for listing, pricing, and reselling tickets with on-chain settlement
Per-event anti-scalping controls including price ceilings, transfer limits, identity-binding, and time restrictions
Custodial wallet onboarding inside Sellout's existing flow
Independent third-party smart-contract security audit with published remediation
Public launch campaign and trade-show activations
Public metrics dashboard and quarterly reporting
Revenue-share repayment mechanism to reimburse the Treasury
request.recipient: Anvil Development Agency, Inc. / Intersect as budget administrator
request.what: Fund Phase 2 of a production Cardano-native ticketing platform operated by Sellout.io and built by Anvil Development Agency, including a secondary marketplace, royalty enforcement, anti-scalping controls, wallet onboarding, organizer tools, audit, and launch campaign.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 4,969,231 ada, approximately $1,093,231 at $0.22 per ADA, over 8 months with milestone-gated disbursement.
Phase 1 of the ticketing platform is already live on Cardano mainnet and was funded by Sellout with over $130,000 of its own capital.
Phase 2 will deliver a secondary marketplace, smart-contract royalty enforcement, anti-scalping controls, wallet onboarding, organizer tools, an independent audit, and launch amplification.
Sellout has 200,000+ registered users, has issued 250,000+ tickets to date, and currently supports 350+ events annually.
The proposal targets 200+ events on-chain, 75,000+ CIP-68 NFT tickets, 150,000+ on-chain interactions, $6,000,000+ ticket revenue on-chain, and 20,000+ new wallets within 12 months from launch.
The Yellowstone Club 2026 concert series is presented as the anchor deployment and is projected to move over $6,000,000 through Cardano in Year 1.
The team commits to repay $1,093,231 to the Cardano Treasury through a revenue-share mechanism using 25% of fees until reimbursement and 5% thereafter.
All on-chain metrics are said to be independently verifiable through Cardano explorer data, policy-ID tracking, and a public metrics dashboard planned for milestone M5.
Intersect is described as budget administrator using the Sundae Labs TRSC/PSSC framework with oversight by six external third parties and public dashboard tracking.
Anvil and Sellout state they have not received ada from the Cardano Treasury within the last 24 months.

summary: The document describes a large treasury request for an enterprise ticketing platform expansion with detailed work packages, milestones, budget lines, repayment terms, and governance-administration claims, but several core adoption, live-status, contract, and feasibility assertions are mostly proposer-stated rather than evidenced in the supplied text.
